CREATE TABLE Equipment (
    Equipment_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Equipment_Model VARCHAR(255),
    Equipment_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Installation_Date DATETIME,
    Installation_Location VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Inspection_Personnel (
    Contact_Information VARCHAR(255),
    Department INTEGER,
    Inspection_Personnel_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Inspection_Record (
    Equipment_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Inspection_Content VARCHAR(255),
    Inspection_Date DATETIME,
    Inspection_Personnel_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Equipment_ID, Inspection_Personnel_ID, Inspection_Date),
    FOREIGN KEY (Equipment_ID) REFERENCES Equipment(Equipment_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Inspection_Personnel_ID) REFERENCES Inspection_Personnel(Inspection_Personnel_ID)
);

Equipment Inspection Management System Functionality:

The primary function of the Equipment Inspection Management System is to manage the inspection records of equipment, ensuring normal operation and timely maintenance of the equipment. The system supports the entry of basic equipment information, management of inspection personnel, and records the specific data of each equipment inspection. Below is the detailed business description:

Equipment Management:

The system is capable of managing the basic information of the equipment, including the equipment name, model, installation location, and installation date. Equipment is uniquely identified by an equipment ID, ensuring the completeness and traceability of equipment information.

Inspection Personnel Management:

The system can record the basic information of inspection personnel, including name, department, and contact information. Managing inspection personnel helps ensure that each piece of equipment has designated personnel responsible for inspection, and the related inspection records can be tracked via the inspection personnel ID.

Inspection Record Tracking:

The system is able to record each inspection of the equipment, including detailed information such as the inspection personnel, inspection date, and inspection content. Each inspection record is associated with an equipment ID, inspection personnel ID, and inspection date to effectively track and manage the status of the equipment. These records allow management personnel to timely understand the inspection status of equipment, identify potential problems, and take measures.

The system ensures timely inspections of equipment by comprehensively managing equipment information, inspection personnel, and inspection records, reducing the likelihood of malfunctions, and enhancing the efficiency and safety of equipment management.

The database name is rschema_0058. It contains three tables: Equipment, Inspection_Personnel, and Inspection_Record.
The Equipment table has five columns: Equipment_ID, Equipment_Model, Equipment_Name, Installation_Date, and Installation_Location. The Equipment_ID column is the primary key and is an integer. The Equipment_Model, Equipment_Name, Installation_Date, and Installation_Location columns are all strings. The Installation_Date column is a datetime.
The Inspection_Personnel table has four columns: Contact_Information, Department, Inspection_Personnel_ID, and Name. The Inspection_Personnel_ID column is the primary key and is an integer. The Contact_Information, Department, and Name columns are all strings.
The Inspection_Record table has five columns: Equipment_ID, Inspection_Content, Inspection_Date, Inspection_Personnel_ID, and PRIMARY KEY (Equipment_ID, Inspection_Personnel_ID, Inspection_Date). The Equipment_ID column is an integer and is not null. The Inspection_Content column is a string. The Inspection_Date column is a datetime. The Inspection_Personnel_ID column is an integer and is not null. The PRIMARY KEY constraint is a composite key made up of the Equipment_ID, Inspection_Personnel_ID, and Inspection_Date columns.
The Inspection_Record table has two foreign key constraints: one referencing the Equipment table and the other referencing the Inspection_Personnel table. The foreign key constraints have update and delete rules of CASCADE.
